note: Draft. Top-level categories 1-4 and 6 are the user's proposal; STRUCTURAL holds non-causal changes (so nothing is forced into a causal box). Subtypes are free to be merged/split after the first full pass; every labelled record stores the taxonomy version it was labelled under. v0.1 adds SEMANTIC_WORDING. v0.2 adds NOT_A_CHANGE/edition_artefact (difference caused by an unreliable, misdated, mis-transcribed or printer's-variant edition). v0.3 adds RELOCATION (user request 2026-10-28).

NOVEL_EVENT.definition: A new on-field event, tactic or situation that had not arisen before (or not in this form) prompts a rule: e.g. the first wide bat, the first round-arm bowler, a famous umpiring incident.

EXTERNAL_FORCE.definition: A force from outside the game itself: technology, equipment manufacture, pitch-preparation technology, medicine/safety, law/society, dress/fashion.

ECONOMY.definition: Changes whose purpose is the economy of the sport: betting and stakes, time per match/over, fixtures, professionalism, cost.

ENJOYMENT.definition: Changes to improve how the game plays or is watched: balance between bowler and batsman, fewer draws / more decisive results, quality of play, fairness and the spirit of the game.

STRUCTURAL.definition: Non-causal changes to the Laws themselves: codifying or defining existing practice, clarifying for umpires, reorganising, restoring omissions, adding flexibility for different conditions, consequential adjustments.

UNCATEGORISED.definition: The source gives no cause and none is inferable from it. Left unlabelled on purpose rather than guessed; candidate for 'random event' once evidence is exhausted.

BASELINE.definition: Not a change: a statement of the 1744 starting position (Rait Kerr serials 1-21).

NOT_A_CHANGE.definition: The text differs only because of transcription: punctuation, quote marks, hyphenation, list numbers, sentence splitting, OCR layout, or a value that the AI clean-up step invented (checked against raw OCR and independent transcriptions). Not a change to the Laws.

SEMANTIC_WORDING.definition: A re-write of wording that does not necessarily change what the rule requires, but may change how it is read or enforced (strength words may/must/shall, qualifiers, pronouns and gender-neutral drafting, terminology). Added at the user's request (2026-10-27). Rows in this category, and rows flagged semantic_only, are excluded from the substantive-changes dataset.

RELOCATION.definition: Material of the Laws is moved within the book - between Laws, sections or notes - so that the structure of the rule book changes. Counted as a substantive change. pure_relocation = text moved or renumbered with no merge or split; split = one Law/section divided into several; merge = several Laws/sections combined into one (or a Law dissolved into others). A move that also changes the rule keeps the rule-change category as primary and records RELOCATION as secondary.

basis_values.inferred: the source implies the cause (context, section theme, 'no doubt')
basis_values.attributed: recollection or claim attributed to a named person
basis_values.derived: established mechanically from the text itself (token-level comparison or comparison with an independent transcription)

cross_cutting_pattern: Rait Kerr's own theme: legislation 1798-1947 was consistently directed at keeping a balance between bowler and batsman; improved pitches (mowing machine, heavy roller, marl) are the root cause he gives for 1884-1947. Consider promoting bowler_batsman_balance to a top-level category in v1.
